$comment: Machine-readable half of docs/plans/flows-canvas-implementation-plan.md. Conformance is enforced by backend/tests/flows-canvas-plan.test.js: every taxonomy node must have exactly one binding whose port contract matches, every 'existing'/'modified' path must be on disk, every 'new' path must be free, and migrations must be numbered above db/migrations/.

phases.name: Shared payload builders
phases.goal: One payload construction path for every capability, used by both the per-domain routes and the orchestrator. Fixes the stub-payload bypass at routes/pipeline.js:122 and the hard-coded ImageGen fetch at routes/storyboard.js:97.
phases.exit_criterion: For every capability, routes/pipeline.js and the matching per-domain route produce a byte-identical payload for the same shot, asserted by a set-based test iterating STEP_CAPABILITY. No route constructs a provider payload inline.

phases.name: Graph as data
phases.goal: Flows, nodes, and edges become rows. The current 9-step pipeline is seeded as a built-in read-only flow.
phases.exit_criterion: buildStepPlan() output for the seeded built-in flow is deep-equal to the output derived from PIPELINE_STEPS, proving the DB graph reproduces the constant exactly.

phases.name: Typed-port executor
phases.goal: executeNode(node, inputs, ctx) replaces executeStep(). Edges carry typed values instead of implying a DB re-read.
phases.exit_criterion: Every one of the 23 taxonomy nodes resolves to a registered handler at runtime, and port-type validation rejects an incompatible edge server-side.

phases.name: Fan-out and select
phases.goal: One node produces N branches; downstream nodes run once per branch; a select node collapses back to one.
phases.exit_criterion: A flow with a fanout(n=3) feeding a generator produces 3 node-runs sharing a branch key, and the budget guard refuses the run when projected cost exceeds the project limit.

phases.name: Canvas UI
phases.goal: A hand-rolled SVG canvas on a new 'flows' sidebar page, painting live node status off the existing SSE stream.
phases.exit_criterion: A flow can be authored, saved, run, and watched entirely from the SPA, with no new build step and index.html still deployable as a single file.

phases.name: Built-in templates
phases.goal: Ship the flows Artlist ships, expressed in Film Engine's domain.
phases.exit_criterion: Every declared template instantiates into a graph that passes validateGraph() with zero errors.

modules.contract: buildCapabilityPayload(capability, ctx) -> { payload, meta }. ctx = { project, scene, shot, sceneCard, overrides }. Dispatches to the existing pure prompt builders and then applies consistency context. Pure apart from the DB reads inside loadShotContext(), so it is unit-testable without a server. Implemented in Phase 0; also exports imageRequestPayload (the single definition of an /image request body) and providerConfigOf.
modules.rationale: The six generation routes each repeat load-context -> build-payload -> apply-consistency -> resolveGenerator().generate() -> persistProviderMedia(). Extracting stages 2-3 is the smallest change that both fixes the orchestrator bypass and gives the node executor something to call. Doing it in phase 0 means phases 1-5 add no new payload logic.

modules.contract: Pure graph algebra over { nodes: [{id, type, config, x, y}], edges: [{from, fromPort, to, toPort}] }. validateGraph -> { ok, errors: [{code, nodeId?, edgeId?, message}] }. nextNodes(graph, completedIds, skipIds) mirrors pipeline-engine.getNextSteps() so the two can be diffed during phase 1.
modules.rationale: Kept free of DB and HTTP for the same reason pipeline-engine.js is: it is the piece most worth unit-testing exhaustively, and cycle detection is the correctness risk that user-authored graphs introduce and the hard-coded DAG never had.

modules.contract: seedBuiltinFlows(db) is idempotent; called from server.js after ensureSchema(). pipelineStepsAsGraph() converts PIPELINE_STEPS into { nodes, edges } so the seed is derived from the constant, not transcribed from it.
modules.rationale: Deriving rather than transcribing is what makes the phase-1 exit criterion meaningful: if PIPELINE_STEPS changes, the seed changes with it and the equivalence test still holds.

modules.contract: executeNode(node, inputs, ctx) -> { ok, outputs: {port: {type, value}}, error?, providerId? }. resolveNodeInputs(graph, nodeId, outputsSoFar) gathers upstream port values. runFlow walks nextNodes() until the frontier is empty, persisting each node-run.
modules.rationale: This is the generalization of routes/pipeline.js:executeStep(). Keeping it in lib/ rather than routes/ mirrors how pipeline-engine.js is split from routes/pipeline.js, and lets a flow be run from a route, a batch job, or a test with no HTTP.

modules.contract: Auto-loads every sibling .js file and registers each module's exported handlers by node id, exactly like lib/providers/index.js:_autoload(). handlerFor(nodeType) -> { execute(node, inputs, ctx), inputs, outputs, capability? }.
modules.rationale: Reusing the provider registry's filename-autoload pattern means adding a node type is one new file and never an edit to a central switch — the same property that keeps provider work conflict-free.

modules.contract: Source nodes: in.prompt (literal + {{interpolation}} from upstream text), in.asset (film_assets lookup), in.subject (consistency profile -> subject port), in.scene (scene_card_yaml -> text + subject).
modules.rationale: Grouped by kind rather than one file per node because these five share context loading and none of them call a generator.

modules.contract: One generic execute() serving all ten gen.* nodes: reads node.capability, calls buildCapabilityPayload(), then resolveGenerator(capability, projectConfig).generate(), then persistCapabilityResult(). Per-node config (model, seed, provider override) rides on node.config.
modules.rationale: The capability is data, so ten node types need one implementation — the same insight that already makes routes/pipeline.js:executeStep() four lines long. A per-node provider override is what delivers Flows' 'multi-model' headline with no new provider work.

modules.contract: tf.mix -> lib/audio-mixer.buildMixPayload/calculateDucking; tf.stitch -> lib/video-stitcher.planClips/buildStitchPayload; tf.encode -> the post capability with an encode profile.
modules.rationale: These three already exist as pure functions with unit tests, so the handler is an adapter, not an implementation.

modules.contract: tf.fanout emits N branch contexts from one input (varying seed, prompt, or provider) and is the only handler allowed to widen the frontier; tf.select is a human gate that parks the run in 'paused' until a branch is chosen.
modules.rationale: Isolated in its own file because these are the only two handlers the executor treats specially — everything else is one-in-one-out, and mixing branch semantics into generate.js would make the common path pay for the rare one.

modules.contract: out.asset registers the value in film_assets via lib/file-storage + provider-media; out.assembly hands off to routes/nle-export; out.timeline emits FCPXML/EDL/Premiere XML.
modules.rationale: out.asset is the load-bearing one: without it canvas output becomes a side channel that the QA checker, budget ledger, and NLE export cannot see.

modules.contract: instantiate(templateId, { projectId, sceneId?, shotId? }) -> { nodes, edges } ready for POST /film/projects/:id/flows. Templates are data, validated by validateGraph() at load.
modules.rationale: Templates as data rather than seeded rows keeps them versioned with the code and lets validateGraph() police them in CI instead of at first use.

modules.contract: handleFlows(req, res, parts, query) — matches the handleX(req, res, parts, query) signature every other route module in server.js uses.
modules.rationale: Follows ADR-002: one exported handler, dispatched from server.js by parts[1], no framework.

modules.contract: executeStep() stops constructing { shot_id, scene_id, project_id, step } inline and calls buildCapabilityPayload(capability, ctx) instead. In phase 2 it delegates to flow-executor for the seeded built-in flow. Phase 6: also persists each step's output, closing the gap where orchestrated runs generated media and discarded it.
modules.rationale: This is the defect: routes/storyboard.js:581 builds a real prompt while routes/pipeline.js:122 ships a four-key stub to the same endpoint, so every orchestrated run silently generates from an empty prompt.

modules.contract: callImageGen() is replaced by resolveGenerator('image', projectConfig).generate('image', payload); payload construction moves to capability-payloads.js.
modules.rationale: Second defect: routes/storyboard.js:97 calls fetch(GRIDLIGHT_URL + '/image') directly, so a project whose provider_config sets image=runway or image=openai still gets Gridlight for every storyboard. The provider layer is bypassed entirely on the one path users see first.

modules.contract: require handleFlows; dispatch parts[1] === 'flows' | 'flow-runs' | 'flow-templates'; call seedBuiltinFlows(db) after ensureSchema().
modules.rationale: Same require-and-dispatch pattern as the other 33 route modules; no new abstraction.

modules.contract: New nav-item data-page="flows" wired through navigateTo(); FlowCanvas is a self-contained SVG editor (pan/zoom, drag nodes, bezier edges between typed ports, marquee select, delete) painting node status from the run SSE stream. Shipped in Phase 4.
modules.rationale: Hand-rolled SVG rather than React Flow because gridlight.json pins build.target=single-html and the SPA has no bundler; the required interaction set is small enough that a dependency would cost more than it saves.

modules.contract: Read-only source of truth for the built-in flow seed; not deleted, so the legacy pipeline keeps working through phase 5.
modules.rationale: Deleting the constant before the canvas is proven would make phase 1 irreversible for no gain.

modules.contract: Unchanged. Node handlers pass node.config.provider as a per-node override layered over the project config.
modules.rationale: Per-node model choice needs no provider-layer change — only a different config object at the call site.

modules.contract: Unchanged. The node palette is validated against CAPABILITIES rather than duplicating it.
modules.rationale: Single source of truth for what the engine can generate.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.image.
modules.rationale: Already pure and unit-tested.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.video.
modules.rationale: Already pure and unit-tested.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.voice.
modules.rationale: Already pure and unit-tested.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.music / .sfx / .ambient. buildAmbientPrompt keeps emitting bed_duration_s so tf.mix can tile the loop.
modules.rationale: Three capabilities share one module; the builder table makes that explicit instead of implicit.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.lipsync.
modules.rationale: Already pure and unit-tested.

modules.contract: Called by CAPABILITY_BUILDERS.model3d.
modules.rationale: Already pure; brings the one capability the legacy pipeline never covered into the same builder table.

modules.contract: Backs tf.mix.
modules.rationale: Pure; drops into a handler unchanged.

modules.contract: Backs tf.stitch.
modules.rationale: Pure; drops into a handler unchanged.

modules.contract: Backs out.assembly and out.timeline.
modules.rationale: Pure; drops into a handler unchanged.

modules.contract: Applied inside buildCapabilityPayload() so every path — route, orchestrator, canvas node — gets identity references, and backs the in.subject node's subject port.
modules.rationale: Today consistency is applied per-route, which is exactly why the orchestrator lost it. Centralizing it in the builder is what makes in.subject a real typed port rather than a label.

modules.contract: Backs persistCapabilityResult() and out.asset.
modules.rationale: Already normalizes buffer-vs-URL provider responses; node handlers must not re-solve that.

modules.contract: Unchanged; used by out.asset.
modules.rationale: Existing storage convention keeps canvas output on the same paths as pipeline output.

modules.contract: The pure payload-shaping half of consistency-context.js. consistency-context re-exports these, so there is one definition and every existing import keeps working.
modules.rationale: Not foreseen by the plan. consistency-context requires db/database at module scope, so applying an already-built context forced a database import on any caller that only wanted to shape a payload — including capability-payloads.js, whose contract is to be callable without one. Splitting the pure functions out was the smallest change that made the Phase 0 interface honest.

modules.contract: Runtime node-type registry: ports, kind, capability, pipelineSteps and multiInputs per node type. flow-graph and (from Phase 2) the executor read it; tests assert it matches flows-canvas-node-taxonomy.json in both directions.
modules.rationale: Not foreseen by the plan, which assumed flow-graph would carry the node definitions. Splitting them out gives the canvas a palette source that is not coupled to graph algebra, and makes the registry-vs-taxonomy drift check a single clean assertion.

modules.contract: PORT(type, value) — the { type, value } envelope every edge carries.
modules.rationale: Not in the plan. Built in one place rather than spelled out by each handler and eventually forgotten by one of them; the typing is the point of the graph.

modules.contract: projectedCost(graph) -> {total, calls, byCapability}; budgetStatus(db, projectId, projected) -> {limit, spent, projected, remaining, wouldExceed}. Fan-out multiplies along a path.
modules.rationale: Not in the plan, which named the budget guard as a phase-3 exit criterion without saying where the numbers come from. Split out so the projection is testable without an executor, and so the estimates are visibly estimates rather than buried in run logic.

migrations.sketch: film_flows(id TEXT PK, project_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES film_projects ON DELETE CASCADE, name, description, is_builtin INTEGER DEFAULT 0, version INTEGER DEFAULT 1, created_at, updated_at). project_id is NULLABLE so a flow can be library-scoped and reused across projects — the 'save it once, reuse it everywhere' claim. film_flow_nodes(id, flow_id, node_type, label, config TEXT DEFAULT '{}', position_x REAL, position_y REAL). film_flow_edges(id, flow_id, from_node, from_port, to_node, to_port, UNIQUE(flow_id, to_node, to_port)).
migrations.rationale: The UNIQUE on (flow_id, to_node, to_port) makes fan-IN to a single port impossible at the schema level, so the executor never has to decide which of two competing values wins. Node position lives on the row, following NeonCore's WorkflowStep.

migrations.sketch: film_flow_runs(id, flow_id, project_id, graph_snapshot TEXT, status CHECK IN ('pending','running','paused','complete','failed','cancelled'), progress_pct, started_at, completed_at, error_message). film_flow_node_runs(id, run_id, node_id, status, provider_id, outputs TEXT DEFAULT '{}', error, routing_note, started_at, completed_at).
migrations.rationale: graph_snapshot is the reproducibility fix: render_ledger can point at an immutable copy of the graph as run, so editing a flow later cannot silently invalidate 'recreate this exactly'. routing_note is borrowed verbatim from NeonCore — a provider fallback is not an error and must not paint the node red.

migrations.sketch: film_flow_branches(id, run_id, parent_branch_id NULL, origin_node_id, branch_key, variant_config TEXT, selected INTEGER DEFAULT 0) plus film_flow_node_runs.branch_id.
migrations.rationale: Branches are rows rather than an in-memory fan-out so a paused tf.select survives a restart, and so the budget ledger can attribute cost per branch before the user picks one.
